take_homes: What I tell the AI first shapes everything it says after. Role and facts steer the answer, and the same idea would apply to the HR questions I put to it.
The AI goes easy on its own work, so its report on itself is a claim I check against my own judgement.
I can save what worked as a rules file that someone else's agent could reuse. That might be how a habit spreads from one person to a team.

monday.move: Pick the headcount and roles question as my live challenge and write the three-line handoff note (challenge, first source, plan-first control). I would use non-employee material, not people data.
monday.who: Me alone, then one HR business partner to read it
monday.stop_condition: I stop if the source needs employee data, until I have asked the works council and the DPO
monday.blocker: Employee data in an AI tool needs the works council and the DPO, and I have not asked yet. I also don't know whether I am allowed to connect Confluence or OneDrive.

misconception.why: Nothing in the module touched roles or headcount. Learning that the AI is shaped by context and flatters itself doesn't tell me which roles go, so I still expect headcount to be the first question.

one_line: The first half, where the AI's answer changes with what you tell it, was good. After that it was a lot of repeated filler, and nobody said what any of it means for people.
